transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess what finally made me come in is my eating’s been kind of off the past few weeks. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ll realize I skipped breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then at dinner I’m mostly just picking at food, even when my wife cooked. My jeans are starting to feel a little loose, so… I thought maybe I should ask about it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I mean, a little, I guess. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, flat feeling. Like the apartment feels really quiet, and even picking up my guitar doesn’t really help much. Does that count as depressed?
Have you been enjoying things less than usual lately?

Um… I’m not totally sure. Maybe a little? Like, I wouldn’t say I enjoy nothing, exactly. It’s more like I have to kind of remind myself to do stuff I usually like, and then it doesn’t always land the same way. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Did something stressful happen in your life around the time this started?

I guess the main thing was my wife settling into her full-time work schedule. It’s not like anything terrible happened, and I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t handle that, but this lower stretch kind of started around then… maybe about three weeks ago.
Has this been making it hard for you to get through your usual day?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still doing the basic stuff around the house, so it’s not like everything’s falling apart or anything. But… my own projects have kind of stalled out, and there were a couple musicians I’d reached out to where I just didn’t really follow through. I guess that’s been harder than usual.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?

I don’t think so? I mean, I worry about normal stuff, like whether I’m keeping up okay, but I wouldn’t say it’s been a lot or out of control. At least, I don’t think that’s the main thing. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you been trying to lose weight?

Not really trying to, no. I mean… I wouldn’t mind being in better shape, but I haven’t been dieting or anything. What I noticed is more that my eating’s been kind of off the last few weeks. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then even at dinner I kind of just pick at it, even when my wife made something. My jeans are starting to feel a little loose, so… I guess that’s why I brought it up.
For the past few weeks, have you felt down or flat most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days lately I wake up with this heavy, kind of flat feeling. Like the apartment just feels too quiet, and even picking up my guitar doesn’t really lift it the way it normally would. Is that what you mean by down or flat?
Have you actually lost weight during these past few weeks?

I think maybe a little, yeah. I haven’t weighed myself or anything, so I don’t want to overstate it, but my jeans have been feeling looser. Mostly I’ve just noticed I’m not eating much—skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then kind of picking at dinner. Does that count as losing weight, or do you mean like an actual number?
Have you been sleeping more or less than usual lately?

A little less, I guess. I’m sleeping some, so it’s not like I’m up all night, but it’s been kind of broken up. I’ll wake up around four or five and start thinking about bills or unfinished tracks, and then I don’t really get back into good sleep. So by the time the day starts, I’m already tired… if that makes sense.
Over the past few weeks, have you been enjoying things much less than usual?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I still try to do the usual stuff, but I guess it doesn’t really… land the same way lately. Like I wouldn’t say I enjoy nothing, exactly, but it’s been harder to get much out of things. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Lately, have you been feeling worthless or like you’ve been letting people down?

I don’t think worthless, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, like I should be handling things better, but I don’t know if I’d call it feeling like I’m letting everyone down. Maybe a little here and there, but not in a big way… if that makes sense.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling hopeless?

Hopeless… I don’t know if I’d use that exact word. It’s more like most mornings lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, flat feeling. The apartment feels too quiet, and even picking up my guitar doesn’t really lift it much. But I mean, I’m still trying to get through things, so… I’m not sure if that counts as hopeless.
Over the past few weeks, have you been having trouble concentrating?

A little, yeah. I mean, it’s not like I can’t focus at all, but when I try to work on code or arrange a song, I’ll catch myself rereading the same line over and over, or replaying the same eight bars and still not really deciding what comes next. It’s frustrating, but… maybe that’s the kind of concentration trouble you mean?
Over the past few weeks, have you been moving or talking noticeably slower than usual?

Yeah… maybe a bit. I don’t know if it’s noticeable to other people, but everything feels slower right now. Like I’ll have my laptop open and just sit there for ages before I actually move my hands to type, or even plug in the keyboard. It’s not dramatic or anything, but… yeah, slower than usual, I think. Does that answer what you mean?
Over the past few weeks, have you had thoughts that you’d be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt pretty low, but I haven’t been thinking about hurting myself or anything like that. At least, not in a way I’d describe that way. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
Compared with your usual self, have these past few weeks made it clearly harder for you to function day to day?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still doing the basic stuff at home, so it’s not like everything has fallen apart. But compared to normal, yes, it’s harder. My projects have kind of stalled, and there were a couple musicians I’d reached out to where I just… didn’t follow through when I should have. I guess that counts as affecting day-to-day functioning, right?
Would you say these past few weeks have made it very hard for you to function day to day?

I’d say… maybe not very hard, if that makes sense. I’m still keeping up with basic stuff at home, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But it has definitely slowed me down—my projects have kind of stalled, and I’ve missed some chances to follow through with musicians I’d contacted. So… harder, yes. Very hard, I’m not sure.
Since your wife started working full-time, have your feelings about that change seemed stronger than you’d expect for the situation?

I’m not sure… maybe a little? I mean, it’s been an adjustment, but I don’t know if I’d say my feelings are stronger than they “should” be. I don’t want to overstate it. I guess I’ve noticed it, but I’m not sure how much is just normal adjusting.
Did these symptoms start within a month after your wife began working full-time?

Yeah, I think so. It’s been about three weeks now, and it seemed to start after she’d kind of settled into the full-time schedule. I don’t know if that’s exactly “within a month,” but… yes, that sounds about right.
